title: How does trying more keys change the best score?
question: How do complete-search maxima change under fixed nested key budgets, with the true key absent or included?
summary: Nine source sections and all five budgets compare null search winners with positive controls. Exact recovery and score acceptance remain separate.

scope.representation: First min(240, available) known-reading output rune indices from nine traces; null indices and additive positive ciphertexts; canonical labels for scoring.
scope.procedure: Run complete nested derived-key dictionaries on 32 null/positive pairs per section; retain every candidate score and maximum; separately append the known true key to positive searches.
scope.parameters: Seeds 0..255; budgets 1,4,16,64,256; nine sections and 32 replicates; 147456 wrong-key scores and 288 true-key controls; fixed normalized English quadgram threshold -5.5.
scope.exclusions: No unknown-page test, adaptive search, beam decoder, offsets, alternate signs, language identification or population false-positive estimate.

finding: Null maxima increase with nested search budgets, but no null or key-absent positive search crosses -5.5 in this grid. Appending the true key yields exact recovery and acceptance in all positive controls.
limitations: Fixed dependent controls and a chosen null generator; zero exceedances are not a universal false-positive guarantee. Included-key searches have one additional candidate. Human review pending.
next_steps: Calibrate the complete selection procedure whenever the dictionary, decoder, score or adaptive choices change.
